punchline: James Clear's rule: missing once is an accident, missing twice is the start of a new habit.
thirty_sec: James Clear doesn't expect a perfect streak. His rule is simpler: never miss twice. The first slip doesn't ruin you, he says, the spiral after it does. So on a bad day he'd rather do ten squats or one push-up than record a zero. A study outside his book backs the idea: in Phillippa Lally's research, one missed day barely affected how a habit formed, while lots of missed days did.
